 Tips for Michiganders on purchasing health insurance when open enrollment begins Nov. 1
 The Michigan Department of Insurance and Financial Services is encouraging ACA marketplace enrollees to get ready before the start of open enrollment.
 October 30, 2026
 By 
 Alyssa Burr 
 Pages from the U.S. Affordable Care Act health insurance website healthcare.gov are seen on a computer screen in New York, Aug. 19, 2025. (AP Photo/Patrick Sison, File) 
 The Michigan Department of Insurance and Financial Services is urging consumers to prepare for the start of open enrollment for health insurance policies on Nov. 1, noting that changes to federal law have resulted in an increase in health insurance costs.
 Affordable Care Act marketplace enrollment grew after Congress in 2021 authorized the expansion of tax credits that subsidized the cost of premiums to make more people eligible, which made premiums for marketplace insurance policies more affordable. After Republicans in Congress failed to renew the expiring enhanced subsidies at the end of 2025, marketplace enrollment fell this year for the first time since 2019, health policy organization KFF reported .
 Those who plan to purchase policies through the ACA marketplace will see higher insurance rates in 2027. Insurers attribute the rising healthcare prices to factors affecting the overall economy, including inflation and labor shortages , according to KFF.
 Michigan recently released the approved health insurance rate increases for 2027 : Starting Jan. 1, people who buy their own coverage will pay an average of 14.2% more, while small businesses will pay an average additional 9.6%.
 These tips from the Michigan Department of Insurance and Financial Services can help consumers pick a plan that best fits their budget.
 Gather the documents needed to enroll ahead of open enrollment: These include Social Security cards; immigration documents; income verification, such as a recent tax return or pay stubs to determine tax credit eligibility; government-issued IDs; and a list of doctors and prescriptions. 
 Keep track of key deadlines: The open enrollment period for 2027 coverage runs from Nov. 1, 2026, through Jan. 15, 2027. The enrollment deadline for consumers who want their coverage to begin on Jan. 1, 2027, is Dec. 15, 2026. Coverage will begin on Feb. 1, 2027, for those who enroll between Dec. 16, 2026, and Jan. 15, 2027.
 Watch the mailbox: Consumers should keep an eye out for communications from their health insurer or the marketplace. The Michigan Department of Insurance and Financial Services warns consumers to verify that any correspondence is authentic before sending any important information to the requester.
 Preview the available plans: Use HealthCare.gov ’s window‑shopping feature, which lets consumers compare coverage options, see changes to premiums and subsidies, and preview plans and costs without having to fill out any personal information.
 The year in review: Take a look at your out-of-pocket spending and doctor’s visits in 2026 to help you determine the coverage you’ll need in 2027. Keep in mind any upcoming medical needs or life changes.
 Be aware of scams: Consumers should double check that they’re on the HealthCare.gov website. Some websites look official but are meant to collect your personal information and then sell or share it with insurance marketers who may contact you with offers for health insurance plans that have limited benefits or that do not qualify for financial assistance.
 Get professional assistance: If you need help finding the right health insurance, visit HealthCare.gov or call 800-318-2596. Consumers with questions or concerns about other health insurance can reach the Michigan Department of Insurance and Financial Services at 877-999-6442 or visit Michigan.gov/DIFS .
